title: Threshold rule body
description: sprk_policyversion.sprk_rulebody shape for sprk_ruletype = Threshold (task 025; spec FR-05 as amended by D-16). ONE numeric comparison between ONE column of the subject and a declared number, e.g. a matter whose sprk_budgetutilizationpercent is at least 90, optionally narrowed by the same 'when' scope filter an Existence body allows. Deliberately NOT here, and refused rather than ignored (additionalProperties=false everywhere): arithmetic or a ratio between columns (the compared value is a number, never a column name or an expression), a second comparison, any related entity ('all', 'exists', 'notExists', 'path'), and a variable binding. The column must also be one of the compiler's verified numeric columns (PredicateCompiler.ThresholdColumns); that is a compiler refusal, not a schema one, because a column's type is not in the body. The $defs below are a verbatim copy of existence-rule.schema.json's filter grammar so a 'when' value cannot carry what an Existence clause value may not; a unit test fails if the two copies drift.

subject.description: The subject entity's logical name this rule evaluates against (e.g. sprk_matter).

threshold.description: The single comparison: the subject's own 'field' compared with the declared 'value'. Dataverse evaluates a comparison against a null column as false, so a subject with no value for 'field' never fires, for any operator.

field.description: A column of the subject (a Dataverse logical name). Never an expression and never another entity's column.

operator.description: gt (>), ge (>=), lt (<) or le (<=). Equality is not a threshold.

value.description: The declared literal, a JSON number. A string (including a column name or '$' reference) is refused.

when.description: Optional scope filter over the subject, with the same grammar as an Existence body's 'when' (shared field -> value/operator filterConditions). May be empty or absent: the threshold comparison itself scopes the subject.

quietWindowDays.description: Per-rule quiet window in days after a dismissal before the subject may re-raise (D-13, spec FR-17a). Optional; absent means the 14-day default. Integer, 0..3650.

then.description: RESERVED, and refused (task 022 rework round 3, L2), exactly as for Existence; RuleBodySchemaValidator reports it with its own message before schema evaluation.

filterConditions.description: The field -> value/operator grammar shared by every clause 'filter' and by the subject's 'when' scope (task 022 rework round 2, F7: 'when' previously accepted any object, so its values skipped the per-value rules below).

filterValue.description: A scalar, an array of scalars (e.g. an id list), a single-operator comparison object, a two-bound relative-date range, or a null test (task 061). No variant admits a cross-clause variable reference.

nullTest.description: Task 061 (D-54): a null test on the row's OWN column, written {"null": true} (the column has no value) or {"notNull": true} (it has one). It carries no operand: the only accepted value is the literal true, so a value that looks like a comparison ({"null": "x"}, {"null": 5}, {"null": false}) is refused rather than guessed at, and null is never written as a JSON null (that would overload '=' and '<>'). Exactly one member, so the two tests cannot be combined. Compiles to FetchXML operator 'null' / 'not-null' on the column, in the same AND filter as every other condition.

dateRange.description: Owner decision D-40 (task 024): a date field may take exactly ONE lower bound ('>=' or '>') plus ONE upper bound ('<=' or '<'), both relative dates, e.g. {">=": "now", "<=": "now+3d"}. Compiles to two conditions in the same AND filter -- still one Dataverse filter (CM-3). Nothing more: no third bound, no two lower or two upper bounds, no '=' or '<>', no absolute or numeric bound.

relativeDate.description: 'now', 'now-{N}d' or 'now+{N}d' (N = 1-4 digits), resolved by the compiler against one window anchor (UTC). The lookahead refuses a newline anywhere: this library's '$' also matches before a trailing newline (review F3).

scalar.description: A literal string, number or boolean. Strings MUST NOT begin with '$' -- that token is reserved for cross-clause variable dereferencing (e.g. '$commitment.sprk_receiveddate'), which this grammar does not support (design.md section 8.0.1(a)).
